attacks.claim: The plan makes hosted-only, proprietary Cirrus Cloud the sole sync backend in 5.0 and archives the stride-server image. This breaks the README/charter promise of self-hosting and full data ownership for ~3,000 self-hosted instances. It leaves no self-hostable sync path, and the plan has no migration path, notice, or maintainer/community sign-off for this charter-level change.
attacks.evidence: "Legacy REST sync is removed in app 5.0 ... after which Cirrus Cloud becomes the single sync backend and the stride-server Docker image is archived."; "the server component is available only as the hosted Cirrus Cloud service"

attacks.claim: All users' workout data, including GPS tracks, will be replicated to a third-party commercial cloud. The plan has no consent or opt-in, privacy-policy update, data-processing terms, region or residency statement, or encryption statement. Location and health-adjacent data is sensitive under GDPR and similar regimes. The beta cohort's real data is exposed the same way.
attacks.evidence: "Cirrus replicates to Cirrus Cloud when connectivity returns." / ABSENT: consent, DPA, data residency, encryption, or privacy disclosure for Cirrus Cloud replication

attacks.claim: All sync for ~90k users depends on a single vendor with no exit path, fallback, or portability plan. The free-tier fit is asserted against devices, not users, with 90k already near the 100k cap and no cost model or contingency if pricing or terms change.
attacks.evidence: "Pricing: free up to 100k monthly active devices; our 90k fits the free tier." / ABSENT: exit plan, cost projection past 100k

attacks.claim: The Cirrus client is a closed prebuilt binary under a commercial license embedded in an MIT-licensed app with access to all local data. The plan has no license-compatibility review, integrity pinning, or audit path. The community cannot build, inspect, or stub it in tests.
attacks.evidence: "distributed as a prebuilt binary (iOS xcframework, Android AAR) under the Cirrus commercial license"

attacks.claim: The rollback story is incomplete. Once data is in the Cirrus store, the halt criterion is crash rate only and nothing returns users to the SQLite source of truth. The 3.x restore from the backup would lose post-migration workouts, and the backup is deleted after 30 days and two undefined 'successful syncs'.
attacks.evidence: "halting if crash-free sessions drop below 99.3%"; "the backup is deleted only after 30 days and two successful syncs"; "3.x detects stride-backup-v3.db and restores from it"

attacks.claim: The rollout halt criterion and success metric don't measure the problem being fixed. Crash-free rate does not detect sync failure, lost data, or duplicates, and 'client-reported' sync success is the same self-belief failure the plan describes. There is no telemetry or alerting design for the sync path, and no outage or fallback behavior for Cirrus.
attacks.evidence: "halting if crash-free sessions drop below 99.3%"; "Sync success rate (client-reported) >= 99.5% on beta cohort."

attacks.claim: Migration is called resumable but has no checkpoint, idempotency key, or count/checksum verification. A kill mid-batch can duplicate workouts, which is the exact bug the plan sets out to fix. The legacy REST path that remains through 4.x also gets no dedupe or idempotency fix.
attacks.evidence: "Migration is chunked (500 workouts per batch) and resumable if the app is killed mid-migration." / ABSENT: checkpoint or dedupe key, count verification

attacks.claim: Conflict resolution is unsound. Device-stamped HLC last-writer-wins has no stated bound on clock skew or server validation. The 90-day tombstone window does not prevent resurrection by devices offline longer than 90 days. The tests reference docs/sync-conflicts.md, whose contents are not in the plan.
attacks.evidence: "per-field last-writer-wins using a hybrid logical clock stamped on device"; "Deletes are tombstones retained 90 days so an offline device cannot resurrect a deleted workout."

attacks.claim: Authentication and authorization for the Cirrus sync path are unspecified: device auth, per-user record scoping, and token storage. The deletion flow depends on a privileged admin API credential with no stated custody. Custom-server REST sync has no TLS or cert requirements stated.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: authn/authz, token storage, and admin-credential handling; "via the Cirrus admin API"

attacks.claim: Account deletion covers only Cirrus-side records and ignores the on-device stride-backup-v3.db (kept 30+ days, plaintext with GPS) and the 90-day tombstones. This conflicts with erasure obligations. The backup also has no encryption or integrity check before 3.x restores it.
attacks.evidence: "Account deletion removes the Cirrus user record and all synced records via the Cirrus admin API within 30 days."; "3.x detects stride-backup-v3.db and restores from it"

attacks.claim: The first post-migration sync backfills every historical workout and GPS track from every device against a hosted vendor. The plan has no throttling, ingest-rate, or load-test consideration, and no on-device disk-space check for the doubled storage during migration.
attacks.evidence: "Migration is chunked (500 workouts per batch)" covers only local migration; ABSENT: backfill throttling, load test, disk-space check

attacks.claim: The core claim that Cirrus gives record-level resumable uploads is unvalidated, and the Week 1 spike has no acceptance criteria or go/no-go gate. No alternative, such as making the existing REST protocol idempotent, is evaluated. The 500-person beta is also too small to confirm a 99.5% success rate, and there are no baselines for the metrics.
attacks.evidence: "uploads are resumable at the record level, so a dropped connection never leaves a partial workout" vs. "Week 1: Cirrus integration spike"

attacks.claim: Maintaining two sync backends in 4.x (legacy REST and Cirrus) doubles code paths and the test matrix, with no stated interface boundary. All of this is bundled with a storage migration and a conflict redesign into one 5-week build for 3 contributors.
attacks.evidence: "legacy REST path behind custom-server flag"; "Adopt Cirrus Sync" alongside migration, conflict resolution, and beta in 5 weeks
